answer: Put every earning identity inside a small mutual-liability pool: members co-sign each other's work, and if any member is proven fake, the whole pool's bond is slashed. Honest pools therefore vet new members ruthlessly, and a lone knoll of real history is the price of admission. A Sybil farmer cannot hide in a hollow haven of fake identities, because a pool made only of his own sockpuppets puts all of its bond at risk the moment one is caught, so the cost of faking scales with every identity, and honest strangers will not insure a stranger.
